name: Demoscene Graphics
visualIdentity: An explicitly 1990s demoscene look built around one coherent retro graphics motif, such as plasma fields, tunnels, rotating geometry, or bitmap lettering. Return to a shared motif and relate visual sections to music; avoid piling on effects or switching algorithms without rhythm.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to retro demo pieces, music-driven titles and openers, greetings or credits, and psychedelic, abstract, kaleidoscopic, or spatial passages. Bitmap lettering can carry short messages. Interactive HTML can use a WebGL canvas and optional controls; this suitability is inferred from the visual and motion guidance.
limitations: Dense text during travel, unstable orientation, reduced-motion needs, or a hidden reset that breaks a one-shot sequence call for adaptation or omission. Keep one primary effect per section; avoid rapid flashing. Demoscene style is explicit, while specific formats and topics are examples, not requirements.
palette: Optional suggestion for new work only: background #171629, foreground #F3EACF, accents #906ECC, #D87589, #53ADBD. Use discrete tokens; gradients are disabled. Supplied exact colors, approved palettes, semantic roles, artwork colors, and style color-family limits take precedence. #906ECC on the background misses the 4.5 normal-text target (4.469); the other listed accent/background pairs meet it, subject to checking actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Build procedural effects in GLSL/WebGL with shared time and palette parameters; Three.js supports geometry, camera, and materials. Keep effects rhythmically coherent and return to a motif. For video, derive all states from seekable composition time and precompute sync data where needed. Interactive HTML may map finite scroll progress to a chapter passage or transition; support reverse/direct seeks, keyboard navigation and reduced motion as applicable. Motion recipes are optional and must fit the scene.
audio: No fixed soundtrack or mandatory layer is specified. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and user requirements. Relate visual sections to music; synchronize and mix through the composition pipeline, then check speech clarity, clipping, balance, and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Use authorized task-supplied assets and exact copy; no particular source assets are required. Bitmap lettering is optional. Load local fonts and assets, seed randomness, and cache or deterministically replay stateful simulations. For scroll-pattern transitions, inspect the actual scene and geometry first; do not assume a listed motion fits.
combinations: Works alone when one shader effect and soundtrack carry the piece. Optional pairings: style-105 for verified beat/event timing, with at most one primary effect per section; style-057 for crisp integer-scaled bitmap scrollers tied to the beat grid. Vortex, chapter handoff, orb, storytelling, and glitch motions are candidates only when scene and narrative support them; omit unsupported motion.
productionApproach: Select the style renderer and motion engine for visual fidelity first; GLSL/WebGL or Three.js owns visuals, and GLSL or a seekable timeline may own motion. HyperFrames is the primary video assembly, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline; Remotion is allowed only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a required capability. Neither defines the look. Interactive scroll is only for HTML; video uses deterministic time. Inspect representative frames and the full render.
